claims.claim: in shallow, densely vegetated Chara ponds surface water swung from 12–25 % O₂ saturation at sunrise to 205–235 % in the afternoon
claims.source_value: surface-water minimum at sunrise 12–25 % saturation; maximum in the early afternoon 205–235 % after about 10 h of photosynthesis
claims.location: web page (PMC full text), §3(b) 'Diel dissolved oxygen variations'; Figs 1–2
claims.quote: Minimum oxygen concentrations in surface waters occurred at sunrise (12–25% saturation)
claims.conditions: four small charophyte lakes on the Öland alvar, Sweden (75–2,500 m², 0.24–0.41 m deep, 319–813 g DW m⁻² charophytes); the intensively studied lake 1, 0.30–0.46 m deep; warm days in May and all days in August; surface sensor at 0.08 m
claims.note: The source calls them lakes ('shallow vegetated lakes (less than 0.6 m)'); 'ponds' is fair, but the rewrite should give the depth (under half a metre), since the paper sets this beside 3–5 m lakes.

claims.claim: while the bottom went anoxic at midday
claims.source_value: bottom water turned anoxic around midday and stayed so until 20:00–00:00, when convective mixing re-oxygenated it; in early June 2016 lakes 1, 2 and 4 were anoxic at the bottom from about 10:00 to 20:00
claims.location: web page (PMC full text), §3(b) 'Diel dissolved oxygen variations'; Fig. 3, Table 1
claims.quote: oxygen simultaneously declined by respiration thus turning anoxic around midday
claims.conditions: as above; bottom sensor at 0.34 m in lake 1
claims.note: Lake 3 had almost permanently anoxic bottom water.

tried.note: Europe PMC refused the script; the PMC HTML was used

notes: Mechanism: dense charophytes reaching 5–10 cm below the surface absorb 90 % of short-wave radiation in the top 9–13 cm and damp wind mixing, giving daytime stratification (0.3–1.9 °C per cm) and nightly convective mixing. Surface pH 8.0 at sunrise to 9.4–9.6 in the afternoon. Charophytes survived 24 h of dark anoxia with a 16 % loss of photosynthetic capacity, 72 h with a two-thirds loss.
